case_name: Secretary to Government, School Education Department, Chennai and others v Thiru R. Govindaswamy and others
petitioner: Secretary to Government, School Education Department, Chennai and others
facts: The respondents had been appointed as part-time sweepers by appellants from 1987 till 1993.

As the respondents and others had been working for more than 10 years, they filed Writ Petition Nos. 17468, 17470, 17472, 17473, 17469 and 17471 of 2012 before the High Court of Madras for seeking regularisation of their services.

The said Writ Petitions were allowed by the common judgment and order dated 23.7.2012 with the direction to regularise the services of the respondents on full time basis based on the individual representation after verifying their service particulars from the date of completion of 10 years of service with time scale of pay.
Aggrieved, the appellant preferred the writ appeals which were dismissed.
issues: Whether the services of the part-time sweepers could have been directed by the High Court to be regularized
petitioner_arguments: A direction to regularise the part-time employees itself is contrary to law and the said direction could not have been issued.

As the impugned judgments and orders had been complied with and the appellants are not going to disturb any of the respondents and others, the law should be clarified on the issue so that in future the High Court may not use the impugned judgment as a precedent.
respondent_arguments: As the respondents had been working as part-time sweepers for a very long time and not regularising their services would tantamount to exploitation.
No interference is called for in these appeals.
court_reasoning: There is no fundamental right in those who have been employed on daily wages or temporarily or on contractual basis, to claim that they have a right to be absorbed in service.
They cannot be said to be holders of a post, since, a regular appointment could be made only by making appointments consistent with the requirements of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The question of giving them equal pay for equal work or considering their case for regularisation would not arise.
Part-time employees are not entitled to seek regularisation as they are not working against any sanctioned posts.
holding: The appeals stand disposed of accordingly. No order as to costs. Appeals disposed of
